To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can use a reinforcement learning algorithm to perturb knowledge graphs in a way that maintains the performance of knowledge graph augmented models while deviating from the semantics and structure of the original knowledge graph.

we have shown how to create deceptively perturbated KGs, which have a significant semantic deviation from the original KGs, but still maintain the downstream performance, and we have also shown that KG-augmented neural models are unable to detect the semantic deviation in such deceptively pertubated KGs

(1) KG-augmented model predictions are highly sensitive to the structure and semantics of the KG; (2) KG-augmentation can lead to overfitting to spurious correlations in the training set, and thus to poor generalization; and (3) the attention over KG information can be easily deceived by adversarial KG perturbations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do KG-augmented neural models behave in a world where the KG is no longer trustworthy?
the following question: Can KG-augmented neural models learn to behave as we expect?
the question "Can we deceive KG-augmented neural models?"

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the attention mechanism in KG-augmented model is not a reliable explanation for the prediction.
we show that, by using a simple reinforcement learning policy, one can produce deceptions in knowledge graphs that are undetectable by the models, while maintaining the same performance.
we show the existence of a gap between the "knowledge" that a KG-augmented model uses for its predictions and the "knowledge" encoded in the KG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to build models that can reason about knowledge, we must be more careful about what knowledge they are reasoning about.
KG-augmented neural models may be vulnerable to targeted perturbation attacks, which may be used to manipulate the models to make predictions that are not semantically aligned with the KGs.
KG-augmented neural models are not as robust as one might expect.
